title: SIGMA: Critiquing More Plates More Dates' Testosterone Booster (feat Gorilla M
summary: A critique (not a product test) of Derek (More Plates More Dates) and Andrew Huberman's Sigma testosterone booster, focusing on marketing, authority, meme branding aimed at young men and the psychology of supplement buying. He argues tongkat ali is the only meaningful ingredient, test boosters are overhyped, testosterone obsession comes from PED users, and lifestyle and training matter far more than pills.
claims: He critiques Sigma's marketing and logic without buying it, arguing you don't need to try a product to judge whether its pitch is sound
Derek's and Huberman's audience is mostly young men seeking father figures, whose blind trust makes them easy to steer into purchases
Anyone who profits from a product should have their integrity questioned, even if their intentions are good
Long 'educational' videos about one's own supplement work like an infomercial: listing every benefit builds desire without ever saying 'buy'
Huberman has promoted digit-ratio claims (finger length predicting testosterone and personality), which he likens to phrenology and MBTI 'astrology for men'
Huberman claimed supplement benefits are felt immediately, but adaptogenic herbs take months and work by accumulation
Discussing natural testosterone optimization with Joe Rogan, who is on TRT, makes no sense
Naming the product 'Sigma' after a meme is zoomer bait; a product that worked would not need meme branding or Huberman's name
He bets most supplement purchases are made with parents' money by buyers who lack judgment
Neither Derek nor Huberman is a chemist or medical doctor, and taking PEDs does not make someone an expert formulator
Every Sigma ingredient has been used for at least 10 years, and the blend itself has never been clinically tested; citing single-compound studies for a combined product is not sound
Tongkat ali is the core of Sigma and the rest is fluff, as with pre-workouts where only caffeine and beta-alanine matter
A tongkat ali extract costs about $10 while Sigma costs $50-60; extra ingredients pad the label and justify the price
Tongkat ali has been sold since at least 2003 and eaten for centuries in Thailand, Malaysia and Vietnam, whose populations are not unusually muscular
Names like ecdysterone and turkesterone deliberately evoke steroids for compounds sourced from spinach and quinoa

Rat studies showing huge testosterone increases are irrelevant; Derek's human data show about 30% more free testosterone from tongkat ali and a claimed ~50% with ashwagandha, both purchasable for about $20
If a pill truly raised testosterone 50-70%, PED users including Derek would drop their drugs for it
Rogan once promoted deer antler velvet spray as boosting testosterone 200%, which was debunked like most test boosters
Adaptogens that regulate free testosterone would be useless to an enhanced user, so an enhanced man is selling something he can't benefit from
The cultural obsession with testosterone was created by PED users; older exercise science gave it little attention
Low testosterone in young men is mostly a consequence of a degenerate lifestyle, which is why TRT is largely nonsensical for young males
Supplements replace positive lifestyle changes: vitamin D replaces getting sun, ashwagandha for stress replaces dealing with the stressors
Exercising, a healthy diet, and quitting porn, junk food, sugar and excess coffee raise testosterone far more than any pill
The best testosterone booster is a good training program; for naturals, training is the center of everything and diet and supplements are accessory
Derek's channel offers almost no training advice, and the only footage of Huberman training shows a one-plate bench
Derek admits he needed PEDs to build a good physique, so his test-boosting advice has little use for naturals
Test boosters are sold under the cover of health, like TRT, but bought for muscle; Derek never mentions tongkat ali's studied anti-cancer properties
Buying a supplement triggers action faking: the purchase feels like progress toward your goal, similar to the reward of compulsive spending
Telling teenagers they don't need your product while linking it is ineffective, since they take the easy route; he compares this to Liver King's practice
Test boosters would only make sense for very advanced naturals, and those are exactly the people who never buy them
Novices credit supplements for newbie gains they'd have made anyway; their testimonials fuel viral social-proof marketing
Influencers create anxiety about testosterone and masculinity, then sell the product that eases it
Whatever the formula or the science behind it, supplements are mostly overhyped, overpriced external factors; real change comes from within
